questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It wasn't too far from home and that the city was a bit smaller.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, there is a lot of information to find on the university website and also intro meetings.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: During the arrivall days, it was possible to get the shuttle bus from the airport to the university building, I know a lot of people that did that, and also there was people to ask questions to etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it through the university, which was very easy and there was many housing choices, varying in amount of roommates, sharing bathroom etc.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In my experience it was nice, because I lived with so many other exchange students, and I had a bike so it didn't matter there was 3 km to campus and the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy, a lot of information was available on their website as well. I received emails about what I had to do in good time. Didn't have any issues I can recall.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The website has a lot of information, and I know that the International office has some drop-in session every week on zoom I think, but you can also just write an email, they respond very quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I applied for, so very successful. Their course catalogue has a lot of information.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in unsure about something or have a question, just send them an email, the mobility office is very helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The overall level was fine, but I did find some of the courses a bit too easy compared to home. But then I also had some courses on another faculty than I'm usually on, which then on the other hand was quite challenging for me. So overall it was fine.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They differed between seminars and lectures, and on my faculty at home we do not have seminars, so this was another kind of teaching than I am used to, which I learned a lot from. Also, I had my courses one at a time, or two at once on half time, which is another way they do the semester in Sweden, and that was very interesting to try.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Development studies 7,5 ects
Development and Political Institutions 7,5 ects
War and Peace one Film 7,5 ects
Environmental Ethnography 7,5 ects

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The course on Development and Political Institutions was very interesting and I learned a lot, but I think the Introduction course to Development studies was a bit boring.
The course War and Peace on Film was nice to try, because it was very different and fun, it however was very easy also. The course Environmental Ethnography was very good, I learned new stuff as well, despite it being an introduction course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: If my deposit for my accommodation is not covering the final cleaning, that would become an unexpected cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol is very expensive in Sweden, especially from Systembolaget.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In Uppsala in Sweden there is a lot of nations, which is these kind of student organisation/clubs you can become a member of. You can eat lunch, hang out and party, everyone goes to these nations, it is a lot of fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The nations in Uppsala hold a lot of activities and events and cultural Swedish parties that is called gasques, where you dress up really nice and is a lot of fun and social experience.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Becoming a part of a nation is a must in Uppsala, really nice to go with your friends or meet new people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Would recommend to visit Stockholm. I also went to Kiruna in northern Sweden, which is very beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, it is easy to meet new people and other exchange students, especially if you live with them.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Choose student accommodation through Uppsala University with roommates! The best way to meet new people. Also, go to the nations, they do a lot of events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Being in a new city where you don't know anyone was a challenging the first days, but then I met so many people, so I didn't miss home so much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nations are very unique and special. Also, the parties/gasques were so much fun and is something completely different than I have tried before.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
In Uppsala the nations make the student life so special and fun, and it is very easy to meet new people and socialize. In the arrival days you can get a temporary nations card so you can try it out.
Get student accommodation with roommates (if you like to live with other people), my roommates ended up becoming some of my closest friends.
Go to at least one gasque at one of the nations, it is a very cultural traditional experience and a good way to meet new people also.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of libraries in Uppsala and they are quite beautiful inside, so you should definitely check them out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Becoming friends with other exchange student from so many different countries and cultures.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home for so long, missing my friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
